papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the interpretability gap in existing module discovery methods and the redundancy problem in pathway-based approaches by providing phenotype-informed annotation of molecular modules. The tool aims to translate complex molecular alterations into coherent biological insights.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined how expression of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relates to semen quality in rams, analyzing 15 ejaculates from five animals. Higher protamine expression was associated with better total sperm motility, and gene regulatory network analysis was used to identify potential upstream regulators of these genes.

papers.title: KBase: Open-source Platform for Collaborative Biological Data Analysis and Publication.
papers.abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy's Systems Biology Knowledgebase (KBase; www.kbase.us) is an open, collaborative platform that integrates data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recently, KBase expanded as a comprehensive, multi-omics ecosystem. KBase enables representation of scientific samples, long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, and scalable modeling of microbial communities across diverse environments. KBase also generates digital notebooks as citable, executable research objects that link data
papers.summary: KBase is an open-source, collaborative platform that integrates multi-omics data, models, and analysis tools to support research in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recent expansions add long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, scalable microbial community modeling, and citable executable digital notebooks. The platform aims to accelerate reproducible, collaborative biological data analysis and publication.

papers.title: Selection favors cost-ordered adaptive mutational paths in a stress-magnitude-dependent manner.
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to stress requires adaptive strategies beyond canonical regulatory mechanisms. Stress varies, both qualitatively and quantitatively, across physiological niches and exerts distinct selection pressures on colonizing bacteria. Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies to withstand various stressful conditions, yet how they tailor their responses to different magnitudes of the same stressor remains poorly understood. We used multiple adaptive laboratory evolution experiments of Escherichia coli across varying paraquat concentrations and genetic backgrounds to dissect adaptive st
papers.summary: This study used adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli under different concentrations of the oxidative stressor paraquat to examine how stress magnitude shapes adaptive mutational paths. The authors found that selection favors cost-ordered mutational trajectories in a stress-magnitude-dependent manner, meaning the order in which beneficial mutations are acquired depends on how severe the stress is. This provides insight into how bacteria tailor evolutionary responses to quantitative variation in the same stressor.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors present a meta-classifier that arbitrates disagreements between ten gene regulatory network inference methods on a per-edge basis, using the raw scores each method assigns to regulator-target pairs as features for a gradient-boosted classifier. They also propose a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts to characterize when and why methods disagree. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a systems biology computational method that leverages longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize promising combinations of targeted therapies. By identifying and mitigating non-response signatures, the approach narrows the vast space of possible drug pairs to those most likely to overcome primary non-response.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a minimal three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, to show that it can simultaneously exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors such as oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map a diverse 'zoo' of behaviors and assess their robustness, challenging the traditional separation of these dynamics in gene regulatory network studies.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating how accurately the inferred network structures capture causal gene-gene relationships. This addresses a gap in widely available software for both Bayesian network inference and structural/causal accuracy assessment in single-cell GRN analysis.

papers.title: Bayesian inference of gene regulatory networks at stochastic steady state.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) form the regulatory backbone that coordinates gene expression. The architecture of GRNs shapes their function and constrains the biochemical pathways through which information flows. Inferring the structure of regulatory interactions is thus essential for understanding biological systems and designing targeted therapies. Despite substantial progress in GRN inference, most approaches-from statistical methods to deep learning-do not take into account fundamental biochemical processes that drive regulatory dynamics. To address this shortcoming, here, we present a n
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: The authors present a Bayesian inference method for gene regulatory networks that explicitly models the underlying biochemical processes driving regulatory dynamics at stochastic steady state. Unlike most statistical and deep learning approaches that ignore these mechanistic details, this method aims to recover network structure more accurately by grounding inference in biophysical principles.

papers.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution enables carbon-negative mixotrophic fermentation and enhanced chain elongation in Clostridium sp. JS66.
papers.abstract: Improving carbon recovery during sugar fermentation remains a major challenge because a substantial fraction of substrate carbon is lost as CO2 during central metabolism. To overcome this limitation, Clostridium sp. JS66 (JS66), an acetogen producing hexanoic acid from glucose, was subjected to adaptive laboratory evolution under autotrophic CO2/H2 conditions to enhance H2-assisted CO2 reassimilation during glucose fermentation. The evolved strain, ALECO2, exhibited CO2 consumption without a lag phase under autotrophic conditions and reached a 9.5-fold higher CO2 uptake rate than JS66. Under f
papers.summary: Researchers used adaptive laboratory evolution to improve a Clostridium strain's ability to consume CO2 during sugar fermentation, creating a strain (ALECO2) with a 9.5-fold higher CO2 uptake rate. This enables carbon-negative mixotrophic fermentation and enhanced production of hexanoic acid via chain elongation, offering a route to recover carbon otherwise lost as CO2.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their associated images, enabling unified multi-modal spatial datasets without requiring shared molecular features or prior annotations. It performs comparably to established uni-modal alignment tools across different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions.

papers.title: Single-cell multimodal analysis reveals enhancer and transcription factor regulatory dynamics during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation.
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes are widely used to model cardiac development and disease, but directed differentiation produces heterogeneous cellular states whose regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Here, we used simultaneous high-throughput ATAC and RNA Expression with sequencing (SHARE-seq) to profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation. Weighted nearest neighbor integration resolved sequential developmental cell states, including iPSCs, mesodermal cells, progenitor populations,
papers.summary: This study applies SHARE-seq to simultaneously profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation, resolving sequential developmental cell states from iPSCs through mesoderm and cardiac progenitors. The multimodal single-cell data reveal enhancer and transcription factor regulatory dynamics underlying cardiac lineage commitment, providing a resource for understanding heterogeneous differentiation outcomes.

papers.title: BioEMMA: Automated Generation of Model-Specific Escher-Compatible Maps from KEGG Pathways.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models are widely used to investigate cellular metabolism, but their interpretation and comparison are limited by the lack of reproducible pathway-level visualizations with a common spatial organization. This study presents BioEMMA, a Python-based tool for the automated generation of model-specific metabolic pathway maps in the Escher JSON format using coordinate information from curated KEGG pathway maps. BioEMMA parses KGML files, map reaction and metabolite identifiers to model database namespaces, filters pathway elements according to an input SBML model, adds non-pr
papers.summary: BioEMMA is a Python tool that automatically generates model-specific metabolic pathway maps in Escher JSON format by leveraging coordinate information from curated KEGG pathway maps. It parses KGML files, maps reaction and metabolite identifiers to model database namespaces, and filters pathway elements based on an input SBML model, enabling reproducible pathway-level visualization and comparison of genome-scale metabolic models.

papers.title: Benchmarking methods for inferring single-cell transcription factor activity using large-scale perturbation sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Transcription factor activity (TFA) is determined not solely by the expression level of the transcription factor (TF) gene itself, but is also modulated by a series of post-transcriptional regulatory processes. Although numerous computational methods have been developed to infer TFA from single-cell transcriptomic data by constructing gene regulatory networks (GRNs), a systematic and unified evaluation of these methods using high-quality experimental data remains lacking in the field. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive evaluation of eight mainstream TFA inference methods spanning thre
papers.summary: This study benchmarks eight mainstream computational methods for inferring transcription factor activity (TFA) from single-cell transcriptomic data, using large-scale perturbation sequencing datasets as ground truth. The authors systematically evaluate these methods across different conditions, providing a unified assessment of their accuracy and robustness. The work highlights strengths and limitations of current TFA inference approaches and offers guidance for method selection.

papers.title: Exact Discrete Stochastic Simulation With Deep-Learning-Scale Gradient Optimization.
papers.abstract: Exact stochastic simulation of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) is essential when discreteness and noise drive system behavior, but the hard categorical event selection in Gillespie-type algorithms blocks gradient-based learning. We eliminate this constraint by decoupling forward simulation from backward differentiation, with hard categorical sampling generating exact trajectories and gradients propagating through a continuous massively-parallel Gumbel-Softmax straight-through surrogate. Our approach enables accurate optimization at parameter scales over four orders of magnitude beyond ex
papers.summary: This paper introduces a method for exact stochastic simulation of continuous-time Markov chains that is compatible with gradient-based deep learning. By decoupling forward simulation (using hard categorical sampling for exact trajectories) from backward differentiation (using a continuous Gumbel-Softmax straight-through surrogate), the approach enables accurate gradient optimization at parameter scales four orders of magnitude beyond existing methods. This bridges exact stochastic simulation with deep-learning-scale optimization.

papers.title: Nanoscale Architecture Can Control Cellular Function.
papers.abstract: Nanoscale protein clustering at the plasma membrane has emerged as a fundamental mechanism for organizing cellular signaling, yet how nanocluster size is actively regulated and whether architectural changes at this scale carry functional consequences remain poorly understood. Here, we used the prototypical membrane scaffold A-kinase anchoring protein 79 (AKAP79) as a model system to investigate these questions through an integrated approach combining homo-FRET imaging, super-resolution microscopy, computational modeling, and molecular biology techniques. We show that AKAP79 nanoclusters respon
papers.summary: This study investigates how the size of nanoscale protein clusters on the cell membrane is regulated and whether changing cluster architecture affects cellular signaling. Using AKAP79 as a model scaffold protein and combining homo-FRET imaging, super-resolution microscopy, and computational modeling, the authors show that nanocluster size is dynamically controlled and that these architectural changes have functional consequences for signaling. The work establishes nanoscale organization as an active regulatory mechanism rather than a passive byproduct.

papers.title: Deciphering the Mechanisms of Statin-Ezetimibe Drug Combinations Using Boolean Logical Modeling and Transcriptomic Data.
papers.abstract: Drug Combinations offer increased therapeutic efficacy and reduced toxicity compared with single agents. Understanding a drug combination's mechanisms of action (MoA) can provide important insights into therapeutic efficacy. The MoA of many FDA-approved drugs, however, often remains unclear. To decipher the underlying molecular mechanisms of drugs used alone and in combination, we investigated the combination of a statin (atorvastatin or simvastatin) plus ezetimibe using drug-treated RNA-seq transcriptome data from the human hepatocyte-like SOAT2-only-HepG2 cells and from liver biopsies of non
papers.summary: This study uses Boolean logical modeling combined with transcriptomic data to decipher the mechanisms of action of statin-ezetimibe drug combinations in human hepatocyte-like cells and liver biopsies. The approach reveals how these drugs interact at the molecular level to enhance therapeutic efficacy, providing a framework for understanding combination therapies.

papers.title: System level identification and multidimensional analysis of hub genes reveal complex regulatory networks underlying human iPSC differentiation into motor neurons.
papers.abstract: Human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold considerable potential for generating motor neurons (MNs), offering new avenues for disease modeling and regenerative medicine. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying iPSC differentiation into MNs, we conducted an integrated bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from the mature Day 28 stage of a publicly available 28-day iPSC differentiation dataset. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using STRING and visualized in Cytoscape, while CytoHubba identified 15 hub genes, including BUB1, TOP2A, AURKB, CCNA2
papers.summary: This study analyzed transcriptomic data from a 28-day human iPSC-to-motor-neuron differentiation protocol, building protein-protein interaction networks to identify 15 hub genes (including BUB1, TOP2A, AURKB, and CCNA2) that appear central to the differentiation process. The findings suggest these hub genes form complex regulatory networks that could serve as targets for improving motor neuron generation for disease modeling and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Integrative machine learning and single-nucleus transcriptomics reveal MAPK-centered neuronal responses underlying the potential Alzheimer's disease risk of GenX.
papers.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide-dimer acid (GenX or HFPO-DA) is a novel per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance developed as a replacement for legacy compounds, yet its potential neurotoxic effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we combined bibliometric profiling, in silico target prediction, in vivo behavioral assessments, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), network biology, machine learning, molecular docking, and in vitro validation to explore the potential relevance of GenX in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Bibliometric analysis revealed increasing research attention to GenX-associated he
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This study integrates machine learning, network biology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing to investigate whether exposure to the PFAS replacement chemical GenX (HFPO-DA) contributes to Alzheimer's disease risk. The authors identify MAPK-centered neuronal responses as a key mechanism linking GenX neurotoxicity to AD-related pathways, supported by in vivo behavioral tests, molecular docking, and in vitro validation. The work suggests GenX may pose underappreciated neurodegenerative risks as a legacy PFAS substitute.

papers.title: Cross-Species Transcriptomic and Network Analysis of Human and Canine Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Identifies a Conserved Replication-DNA Damage Module for Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Rational, mechanism-based drug selection for canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains limited, despite extensive molecular work in human DLBCL. We asked whether human and canine DLBCL share a conserved transcriptional network that could anchor therapeutic hypotheses for dogs. Using public human and canine DLBCL transcriptomes, we derived a 409-gene cross-species module defined by concordant tumour-normal dysregulation and projected it onto pathway and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks. The module was dominated by DNA replication, cell-cycle checkpoint and DNA damage-respon
papers.summary: This study compared human and canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma transcriptomes to identify a conserved 409-gene module enriched for DNA replication, cell-cycle checkpoint, and DNA damage-response pathways. The authors project this module onto pathway and protein-protein interaction networks, proposing it as a basis for mechanism-driven drug repurposing in canine DLBCL.

papers.title: A Scoping Review of Male Fertility Assessment and Treatment Across Historical and Contemporary Paradigms.
papers.abstract: Male factor infertility accounts for up to 50% of couples' inability to conceive. Despite this significant burden, perspectives on male fertility have evolved over millennia, shaped by cultural, medical, and scientific frameworks. Tracing this trajectory illuminates how historical observations laid the foundations for modern andrological science.
papers.summary: This scoping review traces how perspectives on male fertility assessment and treatment have evolved across historical and contemporary paradigms, noting that male factor infertility contributes to up to 50% of couples' inability to conceive. It synthesizes cultural, medical, and scientific frameworks to show how historical observations shaped modern andrological science.

papers.title: SignifiKANTE: efficient P-value computation for gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are graph-based representations of regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes. Various tools exist to infer GRNs from gene expression data, but since GRN inference itself is already computationally intensive, statistical significance estimates are often omitted. While naïve permutation-based empirical P-value computation methods are relatively straightforward to implement, they are prohibitively expensive when applied to popular regression-based GRN inference methods and realistically sized datasets.
papers.summary: SignifiKANTE is a new tool that efficiently computes empirical P-values for gene regulatory networks inferred from gene expression data, addressing the prohibitive computational cost of standard permutation-based approaches. It makes statistical significance estimation practical for regression-based GRN inference on realistically sized datasets, where such estimates were previously often omitted.

papers.title: Trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging for 13C-metabolic flux analysis: evidence-based flux inference under structural model uncertainty.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of intracellular metabolic fluxes is central to systems biology and biotechnology. Flux estimation relies on biochemical network models, with 13C-metabolic flux analysis (MFA) being the state-of-the-art approach. However, isotope labeling data are often insufficient to uniquely support a single network formulation. In such cases, flux estimates become model-dependent, highlighting the need for methods that explicitly account for structural uncertainty. Bayesian model averaging provides a principled framework for this purpose, but its application to 13C-MFA has so far be
papers.summary: This paper introduces a trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging approach for 13C-metabolic flux analysis, which explicitly accounts for uncertainty in the underlying biochemical network structure. By averaging flux estimates across multiple plausible network models, the method provides more robust and evidence-based flux inference when isotope labeling data cannot uniquely identify a single network. This addresses a key limitation in metabolic flux quantification where results are otherwise model-dependent.

papers.title: Immune-Inflammatory Hub Genes Intersecting with a Ferroptosis-Associated Gene Set in Active Tuberculosis: A Multi-Dataset Bioinformatics Study.
papers.abstract: The progression of tuberculosis (TB) from a latent infection to an active disease involves intricate modifications in host immune, inflammatory, oxidative, and metabolic pathways. Ferroptosis represents a distinct form of regulated cell death that requires iron and is associated with excessive lipid peroxidation and has been associated with tissue damage in TB; however, its connection with host transcriptional changes during active TB is not fully understood. This study sought to identify and externally validate immune-inflammatory hub genes among differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in activ
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple gene expression datasets to identify immune-inflammatory hub genes that overlap with ferroptosis-related genes in patients with active tuberculosis. The authors use bioinformatics approaches to find candidate biomarkers linking ferroptosis to host immune responses during active TB. The findings highlight potential molecular signatures that could improve understanding of TB pathogenesis and suggest targets for further validation.

papers.title: YOLOv11-MPD: A Multi-Part Maize Disease Detection Algorithm for Complex Field Environments.
papers.abstract: Maize diseases affecting leaves, stalks, and ears can substantially reduce yield and quality; therefore, rapid and accurate recognition in complex field environments is important for intelligent agricultural monitoring. To address the large-scale variation, weak fine-grained texture, and strong background interference associated with multi-part maize diseases, this study proposes YOLOv11-MPD (YOLOv11 for Maize Multi-Part Disease Detection), a maize disease detection algorithm based on YOLOv11n. The method jointly improves spatial position awareness, shallow detail preservation, local-context m
papers.summary: This paper introduces YOLOv11-MPD, an object detection algorithm adapted from YOLOv11n for identifying maize diseases across leaves, stalks, and ears in complex field environments. The method targets challenges like large-scale variation, weak fine-grained texture, and background interference through improvements to spatial position awareness and shallow detail preservation. It is an applied computer vision contribution aimed at intelligent agricultural monitoring.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal 4D Whole-cell Modeling of a Minimal Autotroph Reveals Central Carbon Metabolism Regulated Locally by Protein Megacomplexes via Post-translational Modifications under Light Disturbance.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central-carbon-metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell four-dimensional (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subc
papers.summary: This paper presents a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4, integrating spatial organization, metabolism, and regulatory dynamics. The model reveals that central carbon metabolism is regulated locally by protein megacomplexes through post-translational modifications in response to fluctuating light conditions. It demonstrates how rapid redox-dependent PTMs and slower expression changes coordinate to adapt metabolism across diel cycles.

papers.title: Immunometabolic Plasticity in Sarcopenic Obesity: Toward a New Paradigm for Precision Immunonutrition.
papers.abstract: Immunonutrition continues to generate heterogeneous and often contradictory clinical outcomes, suggesting that nutrients do not exert fixed immunological effects but interact with the biological context in which they operate. Sarcopenic obesity (SO) represents a paradigmatic clinical model of this complexity, where chronic low-grade inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, anabolic resistance, metabolic inflexibility, and microbiota remodeling converge to compromise the adaptive capacity of integrated immunometabolic networks. We propose that this condition may be interpreted as a state of imp
papers.summary: This review proposes that immunonutrition's inconsistent clinical results stem from nutrients acting context-dependently rather than having fixed immunological effects. Using sarcopenic obesity as a model—where chronic inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, anabolic resistance, and microbiota remodeling converge—the authors argue for a precision immunonutrition paradigm tailored to individual immunometabolic states.

papers.title: Integrated single cell transcriptomics analysis for unraveling heterogeneity and plasticity of root cells for sustainable and regenerative agriculture.
papers.abstract: The plant root system architecture (RSA) functions in anchorage, acquisition of water and mineral nutrients, and exhibits pronounced phenotypic plasticity in response to the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of the soil environment. Resolving the regulatory networks that underpin root development is therefore a prerequisite for improving stress tolerance and yield. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves transcriptional landscapes at cellular resolution, discriminating root zonation, lineage trajectories and cell-type-restricted responses to environmental signals. Coupling scRNA-seq to epig
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell RNA sequencing is being used to map the cellular heterogeneity and developmental plasticity of plant root systems, including root zonation, cell lineage trajectories, and cell-type-specific responses to environmental cues. It argues that resolving these regulatory networks is essential for engineering stress-tolerant, higher-yielding crops for sustainable and regenerative agriculture.

papers.title: HSTXGB: a hyperparameter self-tuning XGBoost method integrating pre- and post-processing for gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Clarifying gene regulatory networks (GRNs) remains one of the central challenges of systems biology and is crucial for elucidating pathogenesis and curing diseases. Various machine learning techniques have been developed for gene regulatory network inference, but identifying intricate interactions is still a fundamental problem. Here, we propose a network structure refinement scheme, termed HSTXGB (a hyperparameter self-tuning XGBoost method integrating pre- and post-processing), to infer GRNs from time-course expression data by leveraging the nonlinear modeling capability of XGBoost while int
papers.summary: HSTXGB is a new method for inferring gene regulatory networks from time-course gene expression data. It combines XGBoost's nonlinear modeling with automated hyperparameter tuning and pre-/post-processing steps to refine the inferred network structure. The approach aims to improve accuracy in identifying regulatory interactions compared to existing machine learning methods.

papers.title: Integrative genome-scale metabolic model of GABAergic neurons reveals metabolic signatures across the mild cognitive impairment - Alzheimer disease continuum.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents a prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the metabolic mechanisms underlying early neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. GABAergic neurons, which maintain excitatory-inhibitory balance and network stability, exhibit early vulnerability during neurodegeneration, although the metabolic alterations associated with their dysfunction remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study builds an integrative genome-scale metabolic model of GABAergic neurons to characterize metabolic changes along the continuum from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease. It aims to reveal early metabolic signatures underlying neuronal dysfunction in these vulnerable inhibitory neurons.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and sports genomics: advancing precision sports science and athletic performance.
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and genomics in sports science has immense potential in the field by enabling personalised, predictive, and data-driven approaches to enhance athletes' performance and mitigate injury risk. Traditional training models based on generalised protocols may overlook individual variations in training adaptation, recovery, and injury susceptibility. Recent breakthroughs in genomics, wearable technologies, multi-omics profiling, and machine learning have produced new possibilities for precision sports medicine. This review explores the molecular and phys
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining artificial intelligence with sports genomics could enable personalized, predictive approaches to athletic training and injury prevention. It highlights recent advances in wearable sensors, multi-omics profiling, and machine learning that move sports science beyond generalized training protocols toward precision sports medicine.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics and network biology in cardiovascular disease: a systems-level framework for translational discovery.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by the complex interplay of genetic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic networks. Traditional reductionist approaches have inadequately captured this molecular complexity, motivating the emergence of integrative multi-omics and systems biology as foundational paradigms in cardiovascular research. This review provides a comprehensive, systems-level framework for translational discovery in cardiovascular disease, synthesizing advances in multi-omics technologies, network biology, artificial
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how integrative multi-omics and network biology approaches can be applied to cardiovascular disease research, moving beyond reductionist single-molecule studies. It outlines a systems-level framework that combines genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic data with network analysis and AI to identify translational targets. The paper serves as a conceptual roadmap for researchers seeking to apply systems biology to cardiovascular discovery.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study integrates computational toxicology with multi-omics data to investigate whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). By combining systems-level modeling with molecular profiling, the authors identify potential mechanisms linking PFOA exposure to liver metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Distinct stage-specific transcriptional states of B cells in human tonsillar tissue
papers.abstract: B cells within secondary lymphoid tissues encompass a diverse range of activation states and multiple maturation processes that reflect antigen recognition and transition through the germinal center (GC) reaction, in which mature B cells differentiate into memory and antibody-secreting cells (ASCs). Here, using single-cell RNA-seq, we identify distinct activation and maturation profiles of B cells within and outside the GC reaction in human secondary lymphoid tissue. In particular, we identify a distinct, previously uncharacterized CCL4/CCL3 chemokine-expressing B-cell population with an expre
papers.summary: Using single-cell RNA-seq on human tonsillar tissue, this study maps the diverse activation and maturation states of B cells inside and outside the germinal center reaction. It identifies a previously uncharacterized CCL4/CCL3 chemokine-expressing B-cell population, revealing stage-specific transcriptional programs that refine our understanding of B-cell differentiation into memory and antibody-secreting cells.

papers.title: Unbiased reconstruction of a mammalian transcriptional network mediating the differential response to pathogens
papers.abstract: Peeking at Pathogen Response Networks Networks controlling gene expression serve as key decision-making circuits in cells, but the regulatory networks that control dynamic and specific gene expression responses to stimuli are often not well understood. This is particularly true for immune dendritic cells (DCs), which respond to pathogens by mounting elaborate transcriptional responses, and are centrally involved in infectious diseases, autoimmunity, and vaccines. Amit et al. (p. 257, published online 3 September) explored the transcriptional response of dendritic cells to specific classes of p
papers.summary: The authors reconstruct the transcriptional regulatory network controlling how mouse dendritic cells respond to different pathogens, using an unbiased experimental approach. They identify key regulators and network motifs that drive pathogen-specific gene expression programs, revealing how immune cells tailor their responses to distinct microbial threats.
